doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

chapter: Early drums, photos and the Laine home
title: Laine's first drums, flags and rehearsals on Charter Street
summary: Laine describes his Christmas-toy drum, field drum and bass drum, the exposition flags, and rehearsing in the basement at Mandeville and Charter.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Is there anything else, Mrs. Lane, you could tell us about the old days when your husband had the bands? That you'd like to add?
I don't know.
You were married, you say, in 1894. Yes. Was Mr. Lane much older than you?
Yes, I was older than you.
Seven years. Seven years.

Oh, I muck with music before I started to play. Before I got married, you muck around a kid, you know, before I was married. I was already about 13 years old, so like that, when I started, you know. I had a drum. I believe it was old man Gilmore's boy. I bought it off of him, a Christmas toy, in other words. That was my first instrument. But the first good instrument came from the expedition. a field drum. They called it a field drum.
Did it have the ropes on it
or the rods? Yes, ropes. Ropes. And my first bass drum, the first bass drum that I got come from Salvation Army, it was roped.
Roped, too.
Leather tongues. It was roped.
What kind of flags did they get from the exposition? Do you remember what the flags were like?
All nations, nationalities.
All different.
Yes. Anything and everything. French, Dago, German, American, all kinds. Anything and everything. Spanish and all. All nations. Yeah.
Where did you have the parade? Where did you march? Where did you have that? Downtown near Spain?
Yes. Oh, yeah. All around the neighborhood. Your home. All around the neighborhood, yeah.
When, we lived on Charton, Mandeville, is when he used to have Raymond Hickey and his sons played with him then, too.
That's where I, that's where I had the most of my rehearsals.
You had all the rehearsals there.
Most of them.
Mandeville and Charton.
Yeah. Mandeville and Charton. Yeah.
I think Dr. Sushon took some pictures of the house.

That's right. That's right. We lived in there many a year. He was a basement. We lived in there for many a many years. And that's where I had my rehearsals. Yeah. It's such a fine place. Beautiful basement, you know. Beautiful. See? I had my rehearsals. Everything that I had in there. I was right on then till War I. That's all.
Yeah.
